title: Father of All Our Mercies, Thou
description: Father of All Our Mercies, Thou in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 470 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Prayer for Grace in Trial”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther of all our mer-cies, thou In whom we move and live, Hear us in heaven, thy dwell-ing, now, And an-swer, and for-give.

lines: Father of all our mercies, thou
In whom we move and live,
Hear us in heaven, thy dwelling, now,
And answer, and forgive.
When, harassed by ten thousand foes,
Our helplessness we feel,
O, give the weary soul repose,
The wounded spirit heal.
When dire temptations gather round
And threaten or allure,
By storm or calm, in thee be found
A refuge strong and sure.
When age advances, may we grow
In faith, in hope, and love,
And walk in holiness below
To holiness above.
When earthly joys and cares depart,
Desire and envy cease,
Be thou the portion of our heart, —
In thee may we have peace.

licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
